model.headline: Released once. Kept for good.
model.body: Each season we release a small number of works, each in an edition of 25 to 100. Once a year, a single 1-of-1 commission. Nothing is reprinted. When an edition sells out, it moves to the permanent archive.

craft.headline: Made the slow way.
craft.body: Every Millwork puzzle starts as a plank. We print, cut, sand, inspect and box each one by hand in our workshop. Tolerances are measured, not guessed. If a piece doesn't seat cleanly, it doesn't ship.

curatorial_note.heading: Curatorial note
curatorial_note.body:
Katsushika Hokusai made The Great Wave off Kanagawa around 1831 as a woodblock print, part of his series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. A wall of water curls over three fishing boats, and in the distance, almost an afterthought, sits Fuji itself. We chose it for the way it rewards close looking: the foam breaks into small clawed fingers, and the deep Prussian blue shifts from crest to trough. Solving it is a slow study of the same image, region by region, until the whole returns.

The print was made to be reproduced. Carved into woodblocks and pulled by hand, it was meant to travel. Returning it to wood feels less like an adaptation than a homecoming.
curatorial_note.link: More on Hokusai and the woodblock tradition

faq.q: I received a Millwork puzzle as a gift. Can I register it?
faq.a: Yes. The registry follows the certificate, not the receipt.
Yes. If you sell or give an edition, contact us and we'll record the new keeper in the ledger.
Your provenance record stays permanently. Early access and invitations pause until you register another edition.

footer.manifesto: We believe a puzzle can be an object worth keeping. So we make few of them, and we make them well: solid hardwood, a clean cut, an image chosen with care. Each work is released once and numbered by hand. When it is gone, it is gone, and the people who hold it become part of its record.
